Implementation Plan

I've written the plan below. It deletes one analysis doc and appends one entry to the processing report; nothing else changes.

**Planning ref:** `c13cc1d13fe7d34391a2a47c33e483ceeb1da4a7` on `orchestrator/project-7973` (the integration branch from the issue metadata; the mismatch check reads `false`).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md` (the existing append-only per-doc subsection format)
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for exactly two things in one directory: delete one analysis doc and append one entry in the report's existing format. No code, workflow, script or test changes. All three implementation issues have merged on this branch: `AUTOFIX_PUSH_TRANSIENT_RETRY` appears 7 times in `review_autofix.yml`, `EDITOR_ATTEMPT_RESULT` 3 times in `review_apply_fixes.sh`, and `DRIFT_SCAN_SKIP` / `not_in_profile` 2 times in `audit_consumer_drift.py`. So the given verdict list stands with no changes. Widening the scope (bumping the stale count heading, tidying other analysis files, adding a changelog fragment for a doc-only report change) would break the issue's "append-only, touch nothing else under `analysis/`" rule.

## Files likely to change
- `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-23-3.md` (delete)
- `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md` (append only)

## Functions or modules to implement
None (documentation only).

1. Delete `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-23-3.md` with `git rm`. Nothing in the repo outside that file references it, so no links break.
2. Append a new subsection at the end of `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`, after the last bullet of the `` ### `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-23-2.md` `` entry (the file ends at line 1506). Keep one blank line before the new heading, as earlier entries do. The format matches the previous entry exactly:
   - Heading: ``### `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-23-3.md` ``
   - The next line: `Processed: 2026-10-23` (today's UTC date; use the real UTC date if the run happens on a later day).
   - One `- ` bullet per recommendation, written as `<ID> (<short name>): <verdict> — <reason>.`. Verdicts are `already-implemented`, `applied` and `rejected`, with an em dash before the reason, as in the 2026-09-23-2 entry.
3. Bullets, in the issue's order. Wording follows the issue's verdict list:
   - Speed 1 (repeat same-head fingerprint guard): already-implemented — the identical-failure fingerprint cap is in place (`REVIEW_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_MAX_IDENTICAL`=3, support-bound markers, non-retryable re-arm, `NOOP_RECOVERY_SKIP_FINGERPRINT_CAP`). A second ledger-persisted counter was rejected: the trusted GH_PAT-authored PR markers are the durable state, and a second store adds divergence. Passing the gate snapshot to the cap job was also rejected, because the cap job's identity-verified read runs only after a trip.
   - Speed 2 (reviewer health circuit breaker): already-implemented — the `REVIEWER_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED` health cache and failback chains, retryable vs non-retryable classes, and the `REVIEWER_MAX_STEPS` / `REVIEWER_TOOL_REPEAT_LIMIT` watchdog. Routing every later pass to failback after one stall was rejected: it reduces diversity, and `REVIEWER_HEALTH_OPEN_THRESHOLD` is tunable.
   - Speed 3 (shard CI lint): already-implemented — by the #4707 parallel job split with the `CI / lint` aggregate.
   - Speed 4 (reduce prompt payloads): rejected — no concrete, verifiable change, recall risk, and README trimming and pre-assembled static context already exist.
   - Speed 5 (ledger substate circuit breaker): already-implemented — the job-scoped breaker in `scripts/ledger_emit_substate.sh` (`LEDGER_EMIT_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED`).
   - Micro (gate phase workflows before dispatch): rejected — job-level predicates already gate, with phase-wrapper parity, and Actions creates the run before evaluating them.
   - Cost 1 / Cost 2: same verdicts as Speed 1 / Speed 2.
   - Cost 3: rejected — as Speed 4.
   - Cost 4 (deterministic pre-classification before xhigh heal diagnosis): rejected — WORKFLOW_HEAL now runs on Claude by default, deterministic routes already exist (identical_failure_cap, non-retryable routing), and pre-classification risks misrouting.
   - Cost 5 (trim memory retrieval): rejected — a micro-saving with quality risk.
   - Semble: informational — no action.
   - Serena probe telemetry: already-implemented — the `SERENA_PROBE` prefix.
   - Rel 1 (catalog lockstep): already-implemented — `scripts/stage_workflow_support.sh` stages `codex_model_catalog.json` from `.codex-workflow-src`, the verified support SHA that also supplies the writer.
   - Rel 2 (transient push retry): applied — bounded transient retry in `Push all pending commits` (`AUTOFIX_PUSH_TRANSIENT_RETRY`, `AUTOFIX_PUSH_TRANSIENT_RETRY_ENABLED`), no force push.
   - Rel 3 (editor failure details): applied — one `EDITOR_ATTEMPT_RESULT` line per attempt in `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh`, with no stderr content.
   - Rel 4 (zero-second failures): already-implemented in part — the collector classifies 404/410 missing archives (`MISSING_LOG_ARCHIVE_MARKER`) and records `startup_failure`. Extra per-run jobs/annotation reads were rejected (§14: they add calls per run).
   - Rel 5 (support provenance): already-implemented — `SUPPORT_REF` / `VALIDATE_SUPPORT_REF` lines and fail-closed pin verification.
   - AI memory duration fields: already-implemented in part (`exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `stderr_category`); the rest was rejected because nothing reads it.
   - GH API audit items and `GH_API_SUMMARY`: rejected — `GH_API_RETRY` already exists, and review-path read consolidation is broad and covered by prior reports.
   - Prompt-cache ordering: rejected — generic.
   - Orchestrator metrics list: rejected — no consumer.
   - BUG-001 (merge without --match-head-commit): already-implemented — every poller merge passes `--match-head-commit` (`ORCH_MERGE_HEAD_BOUND`), and `merge_with_followup` refuses when the SHA is empty.
   - BUG-002 (drift audit profiles): applied — the profile half (`DRIFT_SCAN_SKIP reason=not_in_profile`). The non-`ai-*` wrapper half was already implemented through the `profiles/full.txt` union.
   - API-001: rejected — RISKY_SKIP per the doc.
   - BATCH-001: rejected — NEEDS_VERIFICATION per the doc, and a daily job with low call volume.
   - BATCH-002 / BATCH-003: rejected — RISKY_SKIP.
   - DUP-001 / DUP-002 / DUP-003: rejected — refactor-only (§9) with support-staging risk; `build_semble_wrapper.sh` no longer carries the duplicated writer.
   - EXPR-001 / EXPR-002: rejected — obsolete. The `Stage workflow support files` and `Preflight destructive-commit guard` run bodies contain no `${{ }}`; values pass through `env:`, so the expression length limit does not apply.
   - CONSIST-001: already-implemented — `resolve_integration_ref.sh` uses `gh_api_retry` and exits 75/2.
   - DEAD-001: already-implemented — `BRANCH_REBUILD_THRESHOLD_DECISION` logs `skip_reason` and `last_rebuild_at`.
   - MERGE-001 / MERGE-003 / MERGE-004 / MERGE-005 and REUSE-001: rejected — RISKY_SKIP per the doc.
   - MERGE-002: rejected — RISKY_SKIP, and also already-implemented: clarify's comment read is paginated once and shared.

## Data structures affected
None.

## API or interface changes
None. No identifiers, env vars, log prefixes or workflows change.

## Decisions

### D1 — Leave the `## Processed source docs (127)` heading count unchanged
- Chosen: Append only; do not edit the count on line 5.
- Alternatives considered: Bump it to 128 or recount.
- Why: The issue says the change is append-only, with no renumbering or reflowing. The count is already stale: the file has 64 per-doc `### \`analysis/...\`` subsections, the same number on `isolated-base`, and earlier appends never updated it. Fixing it is out of scope.

### D2 — Keep the issue's verdicts unchanged
- Chosen: Use the issue's verdict list as written.
- Alternatives considered: Re-derive each verdict from the source doc.
- Why: The issue says to adjust a bullet only if the merged implementation differs. A grep on this branch confirms all three applied items landed: Rel 2 (`AUTOFIX_PUSH_TRANSIENT_RETRY`), Rel 3 (`EDITOR_ATTEMPT_RESULT`) and BUG-002 (`DRIFT_SCAN_SKIP` / `not_in_profile`).

### D3 — No changelog fragment
- Chosen: Ship without a `changelog.d/` fragment.
- Alternatives considered: Add a fragment saying the analysis doc was retired.
- Why: This is a doc-only report change with no change to pipeline behaviour, and the issue lists exactly two file operations. Earlier recommendation-processing retirements were report appends only.

## Security considerations
- No trust boundary, endpoint, credential or executable surface is touched; only Markdown under `analysis/` changes.
- §21 auto-close discipline: tracking issue #7973 carries `ai:orchestrator-tracking`. The PR body and commit message reference it only as `Refs #7973`, never with Fixes/Closes/Resolves. This sub-issue may use a closing keyword per §21; the pre-flight `lint_pr_body_auto_close.py` check must pass.
- The PR body records the source doc path `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-23-3.md`, its SHA `39f7c795431f53b24ad73962ee1235e57d5de21a`, and the promote-cycle run https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/actions/runs/39956327837. None of these are secrets.
- Abuse case: none. The report is not read by any automation that acts on it.

## Potential risks or edge cases
- Touching other `analysis/` files by accident (for example `last_collection_timestamp.txt` or `validation-selftest-status.json`). Mitigation: change only the two listed paths, and check `git status` / `git diff --stat` shows exactly one deletion and one modification.
- Any existing report content changing (whitespace, trailing-newline edits). Mitigation: append with a heredoc or an end-of-file edit, then check `g
